message.content:
The bull case rests on record fiscal third-quarter results, with revenue of $1.85 billion up 36.54% from a year earlier and net income of $397 million up 107.85% [D1]. Net margin was 21.51% and income from operations was $461 million, up 97.01% [D1]. The Communications Solutions Group grew revenue 43.09% to $1.35 billion and operating income 86.18% to $458 million [D1]. The Electronic Industrial Solutions Group grew revenue 21.60% to $501 million and operating income 68.48% to $155 million [D1]. Management guided the fourth quarter to revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion, roughly 37% growth at the mid-point, and earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 on a diluted share count of about 172 million [D1]. Demand commentary pointed to rapid scaling of the AI infrastructure ecosystem, wireline orders more than doubling year on year and a growing funnel supporting another record quarter [D3]. The balance sheet showed total assets of $11.92 billion and stockholders' equity of $6.57 billion [D1]. What it needs to see at the next report is fourth-quarter revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion and earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 delivered, together with evidence that supply constraints are easing [D1].

The bear case is that supply, not demand, governs near-term revenue, and management said the supply environment is less flexible than a year ago [D3]. Management expects revenue conversion to be nonlinear over the next several quarters [D3]. One-time tariff impacts lifted fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat, setting a high comparison bar [D3]. Rising test intensity with shrinking design margins forces customers to test at the signal, bit and protocol levels, which raises execution complexity as volumes scale [D4]. Wireline business has shifted away from research and development toward manufacturing as AI data centre build-outs progress, a mix change that management flagged alongside the record quarter [D3]. Analyst tone on the call was slightly negative to pressing, with repeated questions on whether demand is sustainable and whether the outlook is capped by supply [D3]. Investors should also treat the sell-side price targets attached to the story with caution, since such targets are frequently set for reasons other than a genuine view of where the shares will trade [D5]. What it needs to see at the next report is clear evidence that component supply is loosening enough to convert the backlog into revenue, and that margins hold without the tariff benefit that flattered fiscal 2026 [D3].
